items.stem: Define the term “Etard reaction”.
items.answer: The oxidation of toluene with chromyl chloride to give benzaldehyde.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the oxidation of toluene with chromyl chloride to give benzaldehyde.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about nomenclature, structure and preparation of aldehydes and ketones is correct?
items.answer: The C=O bond is polar, with carbon carrying δ⁺.
items.markingKey: (d) The C=O bond is polar, with carbon carrying δ⁺. The other statements are false. With CH₃COCl/AlCl₃ it gives acetophenone; benzaldehyde comes from Gatterman–Koch or Etard reaction. It is sp² hybridised, with a planar trigonal arrangement. Secondary alcohols give ketones.
options: Friedel–Crafts acylation of benzene gives benzaldehyde.
Oxidation of a secondary alcohol gives an aldehyde.
The carbonyl carbon is sp³ hybridised.
The C=O bond is polar, with carbon carrying δ⁺.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The carbonyl carbon is sp³ hybridised.
Reason (R): The carbonyl carbon is sp² hybridised.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: It is sp² hybridised, with a planar trigonal arrangement. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Grignard reagents give ketones with dialkylcadmium.”
items.answer: Ketones are made from acyl chlorides and dialkylcadmium, or from nitriles and Grignard reagents.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Ketones are made from acyl chlorides and dialkylcadmium, or from nitriles and Grignard reagents.

items.stem: What is the product when toluene is treated with CrO₂Cl₂ in CS₂, then H₃O⁺?
items.answer: benzaldehyde
items.markingKey: (a) Benzaldehyde: Etard reaction.

items.stem:
Meera wants to prepare benzaldehyde in the laboratory without forming benzoic acid.
(i) Name two reactions she could use starting from toluene and benzene. (2 marks)
(ii) Why is benzoyl chloride reduced using a poisoned catalyst? (1 mark)
(iii) Name the reagent that converts an ester directly to an aldehyde. (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Etard reaction (toluene + CrO₂Cl₂) and Gatterman–Koch reaction (benzene + CO/HCl, AlCl₃/CuCl). (ii) Pd–BaSO₄ is poisoned so that the aldehyde is not reduced further to the alcohol. (iii) DIBAL-H.

items.stem: Which of the following is a method that gives a ketone?
items.answer: Friedel–Crafts acylation
items.markingKey: (b) Friedel–Crafts acylation is a method that gives a ketone; the others are not.

items.stem: Which term describes the C=O group, in which carbon is sp² hybridised and the bond is polar?
items.answer: the carbonyl group
items.markingKey: (b) The carbonyl group: the C=O group, in which carbon is sp² hybridised and the bond is polar.

items.stem: Name the product and the reaction when ethanol is treated with PCC.
items.answer: Ethanal; mild oxidation of a primary alcohol
items.markingKey: Ethanal (1); mild oxidation of a primary alcohol (1).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a method that gives an aldehyde?
items.answer: dehydrogenation of a 2° alcohol
items.markingKey: (b) Dehydrogenation of a 2° alcohol is a method that gives a ketone, not a method that gives an aldehyde.

items.stem: How will you convert (i) ethanenitrile to butan-2-one and (ii) toluene to benzaldehyde? Write equations.
items.answer: (i) CH₃CN + C₂H₅MgBr (dry ether) → imine salt, then H₃O⁺ → CH₃COC₂H₅. (ii) Toluene + CrO₂Cl₂ in CS₂ → chromium complex, then H₃O⁺ → C₆H₅CHO (Etard); or side-chain chlorination to benzal chloride and hydrolysis.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Draw the structure of 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one.
items.answer: (CH₃)₂C=CH–CO–CH₃.
items.markingKey: 1 mark.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as method that gives a ketone or method that gives an aldehyde: Stephen reaction, acyl chloride + dialkylcadmium, Gatterman–Koch reaction, Rosenmund reduction.
items.answer: Stephen reaction – method that gives an aldehyde; acyl chloride + dialkylcadmium – method that gives a ketone; Gatterman–Koch reaction – method that gives an aldehyde; Rosenmund reduction – method that gives an aldehyde.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Stephen reaction – method that gives an aldehyde; acyl chloride + dialkylcadmium – method that gives a ketone; Gatterman–Koch reaction – method that gives an aldehyde; Rosenmund reduction – method that gives an aldehyde.

items.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH=CHCHO?
items.answer: but-2-enal
items.markingKey: (c) CH₃CH=CHCHO = but-2-enal.

items.stem: What is meant by “the aldol condensation”?
items.answer: The reaction of two molecules of an aldehyde or ketone with α-hydrogen in dilute alkali to give a β-hydroxy carbonyl compound.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the reaction of two molecules of an aldehyde or ketone with α-hydrogen in dilute alkali to give a β-hydroxy carbonyl compound.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about reactions of aldehydes and ketones is correct?
items.answer: Methanal does not give the iodoform test.
items.markingKey: (d) Methanal does not give the iodoform test. The other statements are false. Aldehydes are more reactive (less steric hindrance and less +I effect). Ketones are not oxidised by mild oxidising agents; only aldehydes give the test. It has no CH₃CO– group; pentan-2-one gives the test.
options: Ketones are more reactive than aldehydes towards nucleophiles.
Ketones give a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent.
Methanal does not give the iodoform test.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Propanone gives the iodoform test.
Reason (R): Ketones are more reactive than aldehydes towards nucleophiles.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Aldehydes are more reactive (less steric hindrance and less +I effect).
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Ketones are more reactive than aldehydes towards nucleophiles.”
items.answer: Aldehydes are more reactive (less steric hindrance and less +I effect).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Aldehydes are more reactive (less steric hindrance and less +I effect).

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct order of reactivity towards HCN?
items.answer: benzaldehyde > acetophenone > benzophenone
items.markingKey: (a) benzaldehyde > acetophenone > benzophenone. More aryl/alkyl groups ⇒ more hindrance and less electrophilic carbon.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Benzaldehyde gives a positive Fehling's test.
Reason (R): Benzaldehyde is an aldehyde.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) Aromatic aldehydes do not reduce Fehling's solution; the reason is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Sameer has two compounds X (C₇H₆O) and Y (C₂H₄O). Both give a silver mirror. Y gives a red precipitate with Fehling's solution and a yellow precipitate with NaOI; X gives neither.
(i) Identify X and Y. (2 marks)
(ii) Which of them undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction? Write its products. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) X: benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO); Y: ethanal (CH₃CHO). (ii) Benzaldehyde (no α-H): with conc. NaOH it gives benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate.

items.stem: Write the mechanism of nucleophilic addition of HCN to a carbonyl compound. Why is a small amount of base used?
items.answer: Base forms CN⁻ from HCN; CN⁻ attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon forming a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate, which takes H⁺ from HCN to give the cyanohydrin. Base increases the concentration of the strong nucleophile CN⁻.
items.markingKey: 1 mark mechanism; 1 mark role of base.

items.stem: What is formed when propanone reacts with NH₂NH₂, then KOH in ethylene glycol (heat)? Name the reaction or give the reason.
items.answer: Propane; Wolff–Kishner reduction
items.markingKey: Propane (1); Wolff–Kishner reduction (1).

items.stem: An organic compound A (C₃H₆O) gives a yellow precipitate with I₂/NaOH, does not reduce Tollens' reagent, and forms an addition product with NaHSO₃. On Clemmensen reduction it gives propane. Identify A and write all the reactions. Name one compound isomeric with A that gives a silver mirror.
items.answer: A is propanone, CH₃COCH₃. CH₃COCH₃ + 3NaOI → CHI₃ + CH₃COONa + 2NaOH; CH₃COCH₃ + NaHSO₃ → (CH₃)₂C(OH)SO₃Na; CH₃COCH₃ + 4[H] (Zn–Hg/HCl) → CH₃CH₂CH₃ + H₂O. Propanal (CH₃CH₂CHO) is the isomer that gives a silver mirror.
items.markingKey: 1 mark identification; 3 marks reactions; 1 mark isomer.

items.stem: Which of the following is a compound that undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction?
items.answer: 2,2-dimethylpropanal
items.markingKey: (b) 2,2-dimethylpropanal is a compound that undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction; the others are not.

items.stem: Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between ethanal and methanal.
items.answer: Iodoform test (positive with ethanal only).
items.markingKey: Name of the test and reagent (1); observation for the correct compound (1): iodoform test (positive with ethanal only).

items.stem: Classify each of the following as compound that undergoes aldol condensation or compound that undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction: propanal, 2,2-dimethylpropanal, benzaldehyde, 4-methoxybenzaldehyde.
items.answer: propanal – compound that undergoes aldol condensation; 2,2-dimethylpropanal – compound that undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction; benzaldehyde – compound that undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction; 4-methoxybenzaldehyde – compound that undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: propanal – compound that undergoes aldol condensation; 2,2-dimethylpropanal – compound that undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction; benzaldehyde – compound that undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction; 4-methoxybenzaldehyde – compound that undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a compound that undergoes aldol condensation?
items.answer: 2,2-dimethylpropanal
items.markingKey: (c) 2,2-dimethylpropanal is a compound that undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction, not a compound that undergoes aldol condensation.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about reactions of aldehydes and ketones is incorrect?
items.answer: Benzaldehyde undergoes aldol condensation.
items.markingKey: (c) The incorrect statement is “Benzaldehyde undergoes aldol condensation.” Correct form: It has no α-hydrogen; it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction.
options: Benzaldehyde does not reduce Fehling's solution.
Methanal does not give the iodoform test.

items.stem: Which term describes the reaction of two molecules of an aldehyde or ketone with α-hydrogen in dilute alkali to give a β-hydroxy carbonyl compound?
items.answer: the aldol condensation
items.markingKey: (b) The aldol condensation: the reaction of two molecules of an aldehyde or ketone with α-hydrogen in dilute alkali to give a β-hydroxy carbonyl compound.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of reactivity towards nucleophilic addition: ethanal, methanal, propanone, butan-2-one. Give a reason.
items.answer: methanal > ethanal > propanone > butan-2-one
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order methanal > ethanal > propanone > butan-2-one; 1 mark for the reason: Alkyl groups increase steric hindrance and reduce the δ⁺ on carbon.

items.stem: What is formed when benzaldehyde reacts with conc. HNO₃ + conc. H₂SO₄? Name the reaction or give the reason.
items.answer: 3-nitrobenzaldehyde; the –CHO group is meta-directing
items.markingKey: 3-nitrobenzaldehyde (1); the –CHO group is meta-directing (1).

items.stem: Define the term “Kolbe electrolysis”.
items.answer: The electrolysis of aqueous sodium or potassium salts of carboxylic acids to give alkanes with twice the alkyl group.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the electrolysis of aqueous sodium or potassium salts of carboxylic acids to give alkanes with twice the alkyl group.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about carboxylic acids is correct?
items.answer: Electron-withdrawing groups increase the strength of carboxylic acids.
items.markingKey: (a) Electron-withdrawing groups increase the strength of carboxylic acids. The other statements are false. Methanoic acid (pKa 3.75) is stronger; the –CH₃ group (+I) weakens ethanoic acid. The –I effect of Cl stabilises the anion, so chloroethanoic acid is stronger. They are reduced by LiAlH₄ or diborane; NaBH₄ does not reduce the –COOH group.
options: Electron-withdrawing groups increase the strength of carboxylic acids.
Ethanoic acid is a stronger acid than methanoic acid.
Carboxylic acids are reduced by NaBH₄ to alcohols.
Chloroethanoic acid is weaker than ethanoic acid.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Chloroethanoic acid is weaker than ethanoic acid.
Reason (R): Benzoic acid undergoes nitration at the meta position.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: The –I effect of Cl stabilises the anion, so chloroethanoic acid is stronger. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Write the product when sodium ethanoate is treated with soda lime (heat), and name the reaction.
items.answer: Methane; decarboxylation
items.markingKey: Methane (1); decarboxylation (1).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about carboxylic acids is incorrect?
items.answer: Carboxylic acids are reduced by NaBH₄ to alcohols.
items.markingKey: (d) The incorrect statement is “Carboxylic acids are reduced by NaBH₄ to alcohols.” Correct form: They are reduced by LiAlH₄ or diborane; NaBH₄ does not reduce the –COOH group.
options: Electron-withdrawing groups increase the strength of carboxylic acids.
Carboxylic acids form dimers through hydrogen bonding in the vapour phase.
Carboxylic acids do not give the reactions of the carbonyl group such as oxime formation.
Carboxylic acids are reduced by NaBH₄ to alcohols.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Monochloroethanoic acid is stronger than ethanoic acid.
Reason (R): Chlorine shows a −I effect.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) It stabilises the carboxylate.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Divya measures the pKa of three acids: ethanoic acid (4.76), chloroethanoic acid (2.86) and trichloroethanoic acid (0.65).
(i) Which is the strongest acid? (1 mark)
(ii) Explain the trend. (2 marks)
(iii) Predict whether fluoroethanoic acid is stronger or weaker than chloroethanoic acid. (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Trichloroethanoic acid. (ii) Chlorine is electron-withdrawing (−I); each Cl disperses the negative charge of the carboxylate, stabilising it and increasing acid strength. (iii) Stronger, because F is more electronegative (−I effect larger).

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of acid strength: Cl₃CCOOH, Cl₂CHCOOH, CH₃COOH, ClCH₂COOH. Give a reason.
items.answer: CH₃COOH < ClCH₂COOH < Cl₂CHCOOH < Cl₃CCOOH
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order CH₃COOH < ClCH₂COOH < Cl₂CHCOOH < Cl₃CCOOH; 1 mark for the reason: More electron-withdrawing chlorine atoms stabilise the carboxylate ion; –CH₃ destabilises it.

items.stem: The pKa of C₆H₅COOH is 4.19. Calculate its dissociation constant Ka, the degree of dissociation and the pH of a 0.05 M solution (assume α ≪ 1).
The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Ethanoic acid is a stronger acid than methanoic acid.”
items.answer: Methanoic acid (pKa 3.75) is stronger; the –CH₃ group (+I) weakens ethanoic acid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Methanoic acid (pKa 3.75) is stronger; the –CH₃ group (+I) weakens ethanoic acid.

items.stem: Arrange in increasing order of acid strength and justify: CH₃CH₂CH(Br)COOH, CH₃CH(Br)CH₂COOH, (CH₃)₂CHCOOH, CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH.
items.answer: (CH₃)₂CHCOOH < CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH < CH₃CH(Br)CH₂COOH < CH₃CH₂CH(Br)COOH. +I of alkyl groups weakens; –I of Br strengthens and is greater when Br is closer to –COOH.
items.markingKey: 1 mark order; 1 mark reason.

items.stem: What is the product when ethanoic acid is treated with PCl₅?
items.answer: ethanoyl chloride
items.markingKey: (b) Ethanoyl chloride: replacement of –OH by Cl.

items.stem: Which term describes the anion RCOO⁻, stabilised by resonance between two equivalent structures?
items.answer: the carboxylate ion
items.markingKey: (a) The carboxylate ion: the anion RCOO⁻, stabilised by resonance between two equivalent structures.

items.stem: Write the product when ethanoic acid is treated with NaHCO₃, and name the reaction.
items.answer: Sodium ethanoate, CO₂ and water; acids are stronger than carbonic acid
items.markingKey: Sodium ethanoate, CO₂ and water (1); acids are stronger than carbonic acid (1).

items.stem: Write equations for: (i) HVZ reaction of ethanoic acid, (ii) decarboxylation of sodium propanoate, (iii) Kolbe electrolysis of sodium ethanoate, (iv) reduction of ethanoic acid with LiAlH₄, (v) preparation of benzoic acid from toluene.
items.answer: (i) CH₃COOH + Cl₂ (red P) → ClCH₂COOH + HCl. (ii) CH₃CH₂COONa + NaOH (CaO, heat) → CH₃CH₃ + Na₂CO₃. (iii) 2CH₃COONa + 2H₂O → C₂H₆ + 2CO₂ + 2NaOH + H₂ (electrolysis). (iv) CH₃COOH → (LiAlH₄, then H₃O⁺) CH₃CH₂OH. (v) C₆H₅CH₃ → (KMnO₄/KOH, heat, then H₃O⁺) C₆H₅COOH.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct order of acid strength?
items.answer: ethanol < phenol < benzoic acid < 4-nitrobenzoic acid
items.markingKey: (b) ethanol < phenol < benzoic acid < 4-nitrobenzoic acid. Carboxylate is more stabilised than phenoxide; –NO₂ adds further stabilisation.

items.stem: Which of the following is the weakest acid: CH₃CH₂COOH, CF₃COOH, HCOOH, CH₃COOH?
items.answer: CH₃CH₂COOH
items.markingKey: (c) CH₃CH₂COOH (pKa 4.88) is the weakest; electron-withdrawing groups increase acid strength, electron-donating groups decrease it.

items.stem: What is meant by “bakelite”?
items.answer: A thermosetting polymer made from phenol and methanal.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a thermosetting polymer made from phenol and methanal.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as use of propanone or use of methanal: manufacture of urea–formaldehyde resins, manufacture of chloroform, solvent for paints and lacquers, nail polish remover.
items.answer: manufacture of urea–formaldehyde resins – use of methanal; manufacture of chloroform – use of propanone; solvent for paints and lacquers – use of propanone; nail polish remover – use of propanone.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: manufacture of urea–formaldehyde resins – use of methanal; manufacture of chloroform – use of propanone; solvent for paints and lacquers – use of propanone; nail polish remover – use of propanone.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Bakelite is made from propanone and phenol.”
items.answer: Bakelite is made from phenol and methanal.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Bakelite is made from phenol and methanal.

items.stem: Give two differences between benzoic acid and methanal.
items.answer: Benzoic acid: made by oxidation of toluene; its sodium salt is a food preservative. Methanal: used in urea–formaldehyde glues; preserves biological specimens.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. benzoic acid – made by oxidation of toluene; its sodium salt is a food preservative; methanal – used in urea–formaldehyde glues; preserves biological specimens.

items.stem:
A carbonyl compound or acid has these uses: used in urea–formaldehyde glues; used to make bakelite; preserves biological specimens.
(i) Identify the compound. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were benzoic acid? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Methanal (ii) 40% solution called formalin (iii) used in medicine as a urinary antiseptic; its sodium salt is a food preservative
items.markingKey: (i) methanal – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: 40% solution called formalin – 1 mark. (iii) for benzoic acid: its sodium salt is a food preservative; its esters are used in perfumery; made by oxidation of toluene – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following is a use of methanal?
items.answer: manufacture of bakelite
items.markingKey: (a) Manufacture of bakelite is a use of methanal; the others are not.
options: soaps (sodium salts of higher fatty acids)

items.stem: A carbonyl compound or acid has these uses: used to make bakelite; 40% solution called formalin; used in urea–formaldehyde glues. Identify the compound. Give a reason.
items.answer: Methanal
items.markingKey: 1 mark: methanal; 1 mark: the features used to make bakelite; 40% solution called formalin; used in urea–formaldehyde glues are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a use of a carboxylic acid or its salt?
items.answer: nail polish remover
items.markingKey: (d) Nail polish remover is a use of propanone, not a use of a carboxylic acid or its salt.
options: soaps (sodium salts of higher fatty acids)

items.stem: Why is sodium benzoate preferred to benzoic acid as a food preservative?
items.answer: Sodium benzoate is much more soluble in water, so it mixes evenly into food; in the acidic food it forms benzoic acid, which stops microbial growth.
items.markingKey: 1 mark solubility; 1 mark action.

items.stem: A carbonyl compound or acid has these uses: used to make ethyl ethanoate; used to make ethanoic acid. Identify the compound.
items.answer: ethanal
items.markingKey: (a) Ethanal: used to make ethyl ethanoate; used to make ethanoic acid.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about uses of aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids is correct?
items.answer: Vinegar contains ethanoic acid.
items.markingKey: (d) Vinegar contains ethanoic acid. The other statements are false. Formalin is a 40% aqueous solution of methanal. Vinegar is 6–8% ethanoic acid. It is a food preservative.
options: Vinegar is a 40% solution of ethanoic acid.
Formalin is a 40% solution of ethanal.
Sodium benzoate is used as a dye.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Carboxylic acids are reduced by NaBH₄ to alcohols.”
items.answer: They are reduced by LiAlH₄ or diborane; NaBH₄ does not reduce the –COOH group.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: They are reduced by LiAlH₄ or diborane; NaBH₄ does not reduce the –COOH group.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Formalin is a 40% solution of ethanal.
Reason (R): Formalin is a 40% solution of methanal in water.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Formalin is a 40% aqueous solution of methanal. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define the term “the Clemmensen reduction”.
items.answer: The reduction of a carbonyl group to CH₂ with zinc amalgam and concentrated HCl.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the reduction of a carbonyl group to CH₂ with zinc amalgam and concentrated HCl.

items.stem:

(i) Identify the compound. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)

items.answer: (i) Propanone (ii) used as nail polish remover (iii) used to make ethanoic acid; starting material for drugs

items.stem: Name the product and the reaction when ethyl ethanoate is treated with DIBAL-H, then H₂O.
items.answer: Ethanal; DIBAL-H reduces esters to aldehydes
items.markingKey: Ethanal (1); DIBAL-H reduces esters to aldehydes (1).

items.stem: Which structure corresponds to but-2-enal?
items.answer: CH₃CH=CHCHO
items.markingKey: (d) but-2-enal = CH₃CH=CHCHO.

items.answer: It has no CH₃CO– group; pentan-2-one gives the test.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It has no CH₃CO– group; pentan-2-one gives the test.

items.answer: The C=O group, in which carbon is sp² hybridised and the bond is polar.

items.stem: Which test can distinguish benzaldehyde from ethanal?
items.answer: Fehling's test (positive with ethanal only)
items.markingKey: (c) Fehling's test (positive with ethanal only).
options: Tollens' test (silver mirror with the aldehyde)

items.stem: Which of the following statements about carboxylic acids is correct?
items.answer: Benzoic acid undergoes nitration at the meta position.
items.markingKey: (a) Benzoic acid undergoes nitration at the meta position. The other statements are false. Methanoic acid (pKa 3.75) is stronger; the –CH₃ group (+I) weakens ethanoic acid. The –COOH group deactivates the ring and the AlCl₃ binds to it; no Friedel–Crafts reaction. They are reduced by LiAlH₄ or diborane; NaBH₄ does not reduce the –COOH group.
options: Benzoic acid undergoes nitration at the meta position.
Carboxylic acids are reduced by NaBH₄ to alcohols.
Benzoic acid undergoes Friedel–Crafts reaction readily.
Ethanoic acid is a stronger acid than methanoic acid.

items.stem: What is formed when ethanal reacts with Fehling's solution?
items.answer: ethanoate ion and a red-brown precipitate of Cu₂O
items.markingKey: (d) Ethanoate ion and a red-brown precipitate of Cu₂O: aliphatic aldehydes reduce Fehling's solution.
options: ethanoate ion and a red-brown precipitate of Cu₂O

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of acid strength: Cl₃CCOOH, HCOOH, CH₃COOH, Cl₂CHCOOH. Give a reason.
items.answer: CH₃COOH < HCOOH < Cl₂CHCOOH < Cl₃CCOOH
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order CH₃COOH < HCOOH < Cl₂CHCOOH < Cl₃CCOOH; 1 mark for the reason: More electron-withdrawing chlorine atoms stabilise the carboxylate ion; –CH₃ destabilises it.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as use of methanal or use of propanone: preservation of biological specimens (formalin), nail polish remover, manufacture of bakelite, solvent for paints and lacquers.
items.answer: preservation of biological specimens (formalin) – use of methanal; nail polish remover – use of propanone; manufacture of bakelite – use of methanal; solvent for paints and lacquers – use of propanone.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: preservation of biological specimens (formalin) – use of methanal; nail polish remover – use of propanone; manufacture of bakelite – use of methanal; solvent for paints and lacquers – use of propanone.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The carbonyl carbon is electrophilic.
Reason (R): Oxygen is more electronegative than carbon and pulls the π electrons.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Carbon carries δ⁺.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which term describes the sodium salt of benzoic acid, used as a food preservative?
items.answer: sodium benzoate
items.markingKey: (c) Sodium benzoate: the sodium salt of benzoic acid, used as a food preservative.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about reactions of aldehydes and ketones is correct?
items.answer: Benzaldehyde does not reduce Fehling's solution.
items.markingKey: (c) Benzaldehyde does not reduce Fehling's solution. The other statements are false. Aldehydes are more reactive (less steric hindrance and less +I effect). It has no α-hydrogen; it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction. It has no CH₃CO– group; pentan-2-one gives the test.
options: Benzaldehyde does not reduce Fehling's solution.
Ketones are more reactive than aldehydes towards nucleophiles.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about nomenclature, structure and preparation of aldehydes and ketones is incorrect?
items.answer: The carbonyl carbon is sp³ hybridised.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “The carbonyl carbon is sp³ hybridised.” Correct form: It is sp² hybridised, with a planar trigonal arrangement.
options: The carbonyl carbon is sp³ hybridised.
Ketones are prepared from acyl chlorides and dialkylcadmium.
DIBAL-H reduces nitriles and esters to aldehydes.
In Rosenmund reduction, BaSO₄ poisons the catalyst so that the aldehyde is not reduced further.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of reactivity towards nucleophilic addition: butan-2-one, ethanal, propanone, methanal. Give a reason.
items.answer: methanal > ethanal > propanone > butan-2-one
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order methanal > ethanal > propanone > butan-2-one; 1 mark for the reason: Alkyl groups increase steric hindrance and reduce the δ⁺ on carbon.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Benzoic acid undergoes Friedel–Crafts reaction readily.”
items.answer: The –COOH group deactivates the ring and the AlCl₃ binds to it; no Friedel–Crafts reaction.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The –COOH group deactivates the ring and the AlCl₃ binds to it; no Friedel–Crafts reaction.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Sodium benzoate is used as a food preservative.
Reason (R): Bakelite is made from propanone and phenol.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Bakelite is made from phenol and methanal.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define the term “the iodoform test”.
items.answer: The formation of a yellow precipitate of CHI₃ by compounds with a CH₃CO– or CH₃CH(OH)– group on treatment with NaOI.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the formation of a yellow precipitate of CHI₃ by compounds with a CH₃CO– or CH₃CH(OH)– group on treatment with NaOI.

items.stem:
A carbonyl compound or acid has these uses: its sodium salt is a food preservative; used in medicine as a urinary antiseptic; made by oxidation of toluene.
(i) Identify the compound. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were ethanal? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Benzoic acid (ii) its esters are used in perfumery (iii) used to make ethyl ethanoate; used to make ethanoic acid
items.markingKey: (i) benzoic acid – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: its esters are used in perfumery – 1 mark. (iii) for ethanal: used to make ethanoic acid; used to make ethyl ethanoate; used to make vinyl ethanoate – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Name the product and the reaction when ethanoyl chloride is treated with dimethylcadmium.
items.answer: Propanone; acyl chlorides with dialkylcadmium give ketones
items.markingKey: Propanone (1); acyl chlorides with dialkylcadmium give ketones (1).

items.stem: Which structure corresponds to ethanedioic acid?
items.answer: HOOC–COOH
items.markingKey: (d) ethanedioic acid = HOOC–COOH.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Benzaldehyde undergoes aldol condensation.”
items.answer: It has no α-hydrogen; it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It has no α-hydrogen; it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction.

items.stem: The pKa of 4-nitrobenzoic acid is 3.41. Calculate its dissociation constant Ka, the degree of dissociation and the pH of a 0.2 M solution (assume α ≪ 1).

Assertion (A): Electron-withdrawing groups increase the strength of carboxylic acids.
Reason (R): Benzoic acid undergoes Friedel–Crafts reaction readily.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: The –COOH group deactivates the ring and the AlCl₃ binds to it; no Friedel–Crafts reaction.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Explain the term “Stephen reaction”.
items.answer: The reduction of a nitrile with SnCl₂ and HCl to an imine, which is hydrolysed to an aldehyde.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the reduction of a nitrile with SnCl₂ and HCl to an imine, which is hydrolysed to an aldehyde.

items.stem: Which test can distinguish benzaldehyde from ethanal?
items.answer: Fehling's test (positive with ethanal only)
items.markingKey: (a) Fehling's test (positive with ethanal only).
options: Tollens' test (silver mirror with the aldehyde)

items.stem: Which of the following statements about carboxylic acids is correct?
items.answer: Carboxylic acids do not give the reactions of the carbonyl group such as oxime formation.
items.markingKey: (c) Carboxylic acids do not give the reactions of the carbonyl group such as oxime formation. The other statements are false. Methanoic acid (pKa 3.75) is stronger; the –CH₃ group (+I) weakens ethanoic acid. The –I effect of Cl stabilises the anion, so chloroethanoic acid is stronger. The –COOH group deactivates the ring and the AlCl₃ binds to it; no Friedel–Crafts reaction.
options: Chloroethanoic acid is weaker than ethanoic acid.
Benzoic acid undergoes Friedel–Crafts reaction readily.
Carboxylic acids do not give the reactions of the carbonyl group such as oxime formation.
Ethanoic acid is a stronger acid than methanoic acid.

items.stem: What is formed when propanone reacts with NH₂NH₂, then KOH in ethylene glycol (heat)?
items.answer: propane
items.markingKey: (b) Propane: Wolff–Kishner reduction.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of acid strength: ClCH₂COOH, CH₃COOH, Cl₃CCOOH, Cl₂CHCOOH. Give a reason.
items.answer: CH₃COOH < ClCH₂COOH < Cl₂CHCOOH < Cl₃CCOOH
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order CH₃COOH < ClCH₂COOH < Cl₂CHCOOH < Cl₃CCOOH; 1 mark for the reason: More electron-withdrawing chlorine atoms stabilise the carboxylate ion; –CH₃ destabilises it.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as use of methanal or use of a carboxylic acid or its salt: manufacture of bakelite, preservation of biological specimens (formalin), manufacture of urea–formaldehyde resins, soaps (sodium salts of higher fatty acids).
items.answer: manufacture of bakelite – use of methanal; preservation of biological specimens (formalin) – use of methanal; manufacture of urea–formaldehyde resins – use of methanal; soaps (sodium salts of higher fatty acids) – use of a carboxylic acid or its salt.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: manufacture of bakelite – use of methanal; preservation of biological specimens (formalin) – use of methanal; manufacture of urea–formaldehyde resins – use of methanal; soaps (sodium salts of higher fatty acids) – use of a carboxylic acid or its salt.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Etard reaction gives benzoic acid from toluene.
Reason (R): Chromyl chloride forms a chromium complex that is hydrolysed to benzaldehyde.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) Etard reaction stops at benzaldehyde; the reason is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which term describes compounds used in perfumery?
items.answer: esters of benzoic acid
items.markingKey: (d) Esters of benzoic acid: compounds used in perfumery.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about reactions of aldehydes and ketones is correct?
items.answer: Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition.
items.markingKey: (a) Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition. The other statements are false. Aldehydes are more reactive (less steric hindrance and less +I effect). It has no α-hydrogen; it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction. Ketones are not oxidised by mild oxidising agents; only aldehydes give the test.
options: Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition.
Ketones are more reactive than aldehydes towards nucleophiles.
Ketones give a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about nomenclature, structure and preparation of aldehydes and ketones is incorrect?
items.answer: Friedel–Crafts acylation of benzene gives benzaldehyde.
items.markingKey: (d) The incorrect statement is “Friedel–Crafts acylation of benzene gives benzaldehyde.” Correct form: With CH₃COCl/AlCl₃ it gives acetophenone; benzaldehyde comes from Gatterman–Koch or Etard reaction.
options: Ketones are prepared from acyl chlorides and dialkylcadmium.
The C=O bond is polar, with carbon carrying δ⁺.
The carbonyl carbon is sp² hybridised.
Friedel–Crafts acylation of benzene gives benzaldehyde.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of reactivity towards HCN: benzophenone, acetophenone, benzaldehyde. Give a reason.
items.answer: benzaldehyde > acetophenone > benzophenone
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order benzaldehyde > acetophenone > benzophenone; 1 mark for the reason: More aryl/alkyl groups ⇒ more hindrance and less electrophilic carbon.
